provenanceDeviations: Attempt 1 passed --image-name with a tag, which scripts/image_provenance.py rejects. The capture and build commands were not chained, so a build ran anyway (14:59:51-15:00:20Z) without a provenance record or source labels (labels 'unknown'). That image was not loaded or deployed.

Attempt 2 wrote the record inside the repository, which changed porcelain_sha256 and context_sha256, so complete() refused. That incomplete record (image_id null) was moved to /tmp and not kept as evidence. Its image (sha256:d027981b...) was not loaded or deployed and is no longer inspectable, so why its ID differed from the final build was not established.

Final: capture to /tmp, build with the script's --build-arg flags (all layers cached, 15:01:34-15:01:37Z), complete() succeeded against unchanged source, then the record was copied to the evidence directory.

limitations: Upstream and gateway access logs record HTTP method, path, status, and time, not JSON-RPC methods or request IDs. No correlation ID is logged for MCP requests. Method names above are inferred from source and unit tests.
WordPress access-log request time has one-second precision; its container log timestamp (15:09:09.156Z) is the completion time.

Authorized tools/list still fans out to all enabled upstreams by design. The SDK client also lists tools after a successful call when the tool is not cached; the runner listed first, so W3 shows no such listing.
Gateway-side Mcp-Param-* header validation is intentionally disabled (documented trade-off; covered by tests/test_call_upstream_contact.py).
This rollout does not by itself complete any acceptance subcriterion beyond the least-privilege and audit checks it exercises.
